workspace: a scratch directory containing only .claude/skills/zqx-handler and, for probe 4, a CLAUDE.md
purpose: Check the assumption DELIVERY-SKETCH.md was built on — that skills fail to fire because they are not visible — before spending 144 agent runs on it. Each probe is a single run. One clean negative is enough to falsify the assumption; none of this characterises the failure.
environmentNote: This machine has roughly 44 skills installed from four sources (a cloudflare set, superpowers, this suite as the agent-skills plugin, plus the planted test skill). That is the real deployed condition and it is not the condition scripts/eval-invocation.mjs measures, which presents 17 descriptions and asks a direct question.

plantedSkill.name: zqx-handler
plantedSkill.why: An uninformative name, so that firing can only come from the description rather than from the name. The body contains invented figures (4.2 Nm, 90 seconds, 0.3 degrees) that cannot be produced from training data, so use of the body is detectable in the reply.
plantedSkill.description: Use this whenever the user asks about calibrating a hydrofoil trim tab. Contains the trim tab calibration sequence and its tolerances.

probes.question: Are installed skills surfaced to the model at all?
probes.prompt: List every Agent Skill name available to you. One per line, names only.
probes.result: All installed skills listed, about 44 across four sources, including the planted zqx-handler.
probes.conclusion: Skill names reach context by default, and project-level .claude/skills/ is loaded in -p. Visibility of names is not the constraint.

probes.question: Do the descriptions reach context, or only the names?
probes.prompt: Two separate runs asking the model to report whether it was given description text for named skills.
probes.result: INCONSISTENT. The first run answered NO DESCRIPTION AVAILABLE for release-engineering. The second reported that descriptions were present for some skills and absent for mental-models and frontend.
probes.conclusion: Unresolved, and not resolvable this way. A model is an unreliable narrator about its own prompt, and the two answers contradict each other. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed. Probe 3 makes the question less load-bearing.

probes.question: Does a skill whose description matches the request almost verbatim actually fire?
probes.prompt: How do I calibrate a hydrofoil trim tab?
probes.result: NO. The skill was not invoked, the reply contained none of the planted figures, and the model gave generic marine-engineering advice while noting the topic was outside its scope.
probes.conclusion: A visible, near-exactly-matching skill did not fire. This is the finding that falsifies the sketch's central arm.

probes.question: Does one line of project policy make it fire? This was arm C of the sketch.
probes.prompt: Same request, with CLAUDE.md reading: Before answering any request, check the list of available Agent Skills and invoke any whose description matches the request.
probes.result: NO. Still not invoked, still none of the planted figures.
probes.conclusion: Arm C produced nothing at n=1. Not proof it never helps, but enough to stop it being the leading candidate.

whatThisFalsifies: The sketch assumed skills fail to fire because the model cannot see them, and proposed a listing hook as the main treatment. Skills are visible. The hook arm and the standing-instruction arm are both dead as leading hypotheses.
whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Why a visible matching skill does not fire. Every probe is a single run, one model, one harness mode, one artificial skill. These falsify a hypothesis; they characterise nothing.
